content:
incident-bot: [ALERT] sev2: multiple pods OOM/killed in runtime pool kv-paged-02 — 3 nodes reporting increasing resident set growth over last 45m :rotating_light:

oncall-ryan: seeing repeated OOMKilled on kv-paged-02-*. Container restarted 2-3x each. CUDA errors in logs too. Investigating now.

sre-ash: grabbing logs and pmap. Can you paste the last failure trace?

oncall-ryan: paste logs:
```
2026-03-17T08:33:12Z runtime ERROR: cudaErrorIllegalAddress at attention_pager.cu:412
2026-03-17T08:33:12Z runtime WARN: slab alloc cluster id=7 size=128MB returned fragmented free -> resident up 450MB -> oom
2026-03-17T08:33:12Z kubelet: killing container "runtime" due to OOMKilled
```

eng-runtime-maya: that IllegalAddress usually occurs when KV page index references stale pointer after compaction. We saw similar slow-creep fragmentation in canaries last week.

eng-ml-kenton: workload pattern? long chat sessions or long prefix recency?

oncall-ryan: heavy long-context chat traffic on a specific model (conv-13b) from a single customer route. seq len distribution skewed high.

infra-jen: node flaps observed — kube reported NodeNotReady for 1m around the restarts. Might be GPU driver resets after the CUDA fault.

monitoring-bot: Metric spike: kv_cache.resident_mb per-pod increased 60% over 30m; eviction_rate decreased 40% (config unchanged). Latency 95p up 180ms; 5xx rate up from 0.03% -> 0.8% for route /v1/generate for keys in pool 07.

cust-ops-liz: customer ops: we are getting 3 support tickets reporting requests failing with 503s and increased latency. No data exfil. Customers impacted: alpha-startup-prod and beta-analytics-prod. Notifying account owners.

eng-runtime-maya: immediate mitigation suggestions: 1) enable aggressive KV eviction on affected pool 2) reduce per-request kv cache retention TTL 3) route traffic off pool to fallback smaller-quantized model variant until patched.

oncall-ryan: can we flip eviction aggressiveness? How?

sre-ash: running command to flip live policy on pool kv-paged-02:
```
curl -X POST "https://ops-api.internal/pools/kv-paged-02/policy" -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPSTOKEN" -d '{"eviction_mode":"aggressive","kv_ttl_sec":60}'
```

monitoring-bot: Policy change applied to kv-paged-02: eviction_mode=aggressive, kv_ttl_sec=60 — propagation to nodes in 12s.

eng-runtime-maya: start rolling drain of worst nodes and cordon so new pods land on healthy GPUs. Procedure: cordon -> scale down pool -> scale up with new config.

oncall-ryan: executing drain/cordon for kv-paged-02-node-7 and node-9 now.

infra-jen: note: driver reset on node-9 means we should reclone kernel module; I've queued a node reboot after drain.

eng-ml-kenton: initiating routing policy to shift 70% traffic off conv-13b@kv-paged-02 to conv-13b-quantized@fallback-pool using smart-routing, will keep 30% for canary.

cust-ops-liz: communicating to customers: alpha-startup-prod seeing intermittent 503s, we have mitigations in flight, ETA 15-30m.

oncall-ryan: after eviction flip and drain we saw resident drop ~300MB per-pod and OOMs stopped immediately on the drained nodes. 95p latency back down ~90ms. 5xx rate decreased but still elevated on older pods.

eng-runtime-maya: root cause hypothesis: slow KV page fragmentation from long-tail sequences + a compaction race that leaves stale references until eviction thresholds trigger. Under heavy long-context load fragmentation accumulates and eventually triggers illegal GPU memory references during page reclamation.

eng-ml-kenton: mitigation roadmap: short-term: eviction aggression + routing fallback. Mid-term: patch compaction to atomically update page indices and add canary compaction testing. Long-term: add per-caller long-session caps and model-level sequence-shaping suggestions.

monitoring-bot: post-mit metrics: kv_cache.resident_mb normalized; eviction_rate elevated (expected); overall 5xx for route at 0.12% now.

cust-ops-liz: posted update to status page: "Degraded performance for some Generation requests; mitigations in progress."

infra-jen: node-9 rebooted cleanly, drivers reloaded. No further driver resets observed.

oncall-ryan: preparing handoff to next oncall. Still monitoring fallback pool latency and eviction churn. Any blockers for handoff?

oncall-ash: I'll take watch — please include the commands you ran and the ticket links.

oncall-ryan: handoff notes pasted:
- applied eviction_mode=aggressive on kv-paged-02 at 08:41 UTC
- routed 70% traffic to conv-13b-quantized fallback at 08:45 UTC
- drained/cordoned node-7/node-9; node-9 rebooted by infra
- customer ops notified; status page updated
- monitoring alert thresholds temporarily raised to avoid noise

eng-runtime-maya: created PR with compaction patch and added unit tests, will try to cut a canary build today. Link: https://git.internal/r/inference/merge/1129

cust-ops-liz: continuing customer comms; will loop in AE if SLA risk increases.

oncall-ash: taking over. I'll watch for recurring OOMs and any regressions after canary rollout. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Manual follow-ups assigned: eng-runtime (compaction patch), eng-ml (traffic shaping guidance), infra (node health sweep).
